clue.text: Like the Prophet's mountain, deaf to entreaty

explanation.surface: A comparison with the mountain that would not come to the Prophet, applied to someone who ignores pleas.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says that if the mountain will not come to Mohammed, Mohammed must go to the mountain: the mountain stayed put.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial mountain stayed where it was, and a person unswayed by pleading is likewise impassive and unshaken.

clue.text: Ancient character was large and round.

definitions.text: Ancient character was large and round.

parts.words: Ancient character was large and round.
parts.note: describes the big rounded capital lettering of early Greek and Latin manuscripts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person from history, but it is a written letter: the script of fourth- to eighth-century manuscripts used big rounded capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncial script is the style of large rounded capital letters found in old manuscripts.

clue.text: Like a German author affecting pipe and tweeds perhaps ?

parts.note: Thomas Mann, the German novelist of The Magic Mountain
the suffix -ish means 'like' or 'somewhat resembling'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a writer resembling a German novelist would sport a pipe and tweeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a woman with masculine affectations such as a pipe and tweed suit; 'perhaps' marks these as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman adopting a pipe and tweeds is putting on masculine manners, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Goddess on a mountain ensnared Tannhäuser

definitions.text: Goddess on a mountain ensnared Tannhäuser

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
berg is German for a mountain

explanation.surface: The legend of the minstrel knight held captive by the goddess of love inside her mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend Wagner set as an opera, the knight Tannhäuser is held in thrall by Venus inside her mountain; the whole clue both builds and defines the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Venusberg is the mountain of the Tannhäuser legend where the goddess kept the knight captive in pleasure.

clue.text: Dealer produces — a motorcar part

explanation.surface: A trader turning out a component for cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produces' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler who supplies goods is one sense; the other is the device in a petrol engine that sends current to each spark plug in turn.

clue.text: How a frog died?'

parts.note: the frog's call and the slang for dying share a single word, so the frog's death is described by its own noise

explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb for dying is the same word as the noise a frog makes.

clue.text: No gent would be seen on an obsolete omnibus

definitions.text: would be seen on an obsolete omnibus

explanation.surface: A remark that a gentleman would never ride an old-fashioned bus.
explanation.walkthrough: On early horse-drawn omnibuses the conductor was called a cad, a sense now obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, and also the old word for an omnibus conductor.

clue.text: Sort of sequence of command

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a kind or class, an arrangement in sequence, and an instruction given by someone in authority.

clue.text: Sea-roving sun-king

parts.note: the balsa raft Thor Heyerdahl sailed across the Pacific in 1947 was named after an Inca sun god

explanation.walkthrough: Heyerdahl named his raft after the Inca sun god and legendary king, so a sea-roving vessel bears the sun-king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kon-Tiki was both the Inca sun deity and the raft that crossed the Pacific in 1947.

clue.text: Erased one's name from the round robin, as planned?

definitions.text: Erased one's name from the round robin

explanation.surface: Someone took their signature off a petition, as was intended.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DE-SIGNED it means un-signed, having taken one's signature away; a round robin is a petition signed by many.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a signature is to un-sign; the same letters as one word mean intended or devised.

clue.text: Given place' in the calendar in a second reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorganises the positions, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was fitted into the church calendar in a quick rearrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' rearranges the letters of IN A SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is given a feast day in the church calendar when officially declared holy by the Church.

clue.text: In a haunt of thieves is a French saint

parts.note: a den is a hideout or lair of thieves

explanation.surface: A French saint is found in a thieves' den.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Denis is the patron saint of France, first bishop of Paris.

clue.text: Woe is me — without one nominal disguise

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the lament is placed around the letter for one

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of grief, like 'woe is me'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cry of grief from someone left without anybody, followed by a hidden name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is its old sense 'outside': ALAS sits outside I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumed name is a disguise in the form of a name, so 'nominal' refers to naming.

clue.text: Going and making fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone heading off and reorganising things.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SORTING it means sorting again.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorting to a place is going there frequently; re-sorting is arranging things anew.

clue.text: It's a midget's odd way of being given a bad name

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of these words come out in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, ITS
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the peculiar way a small person is branded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd way' signals the anagram of ITS A MIDGETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be branded with disgrace is to be described as shameful, the sense of having a stigma put upon one.

clue.text: Mrs Giles's chasers are roundly celebrated

definitions.text: Mrs Giles's chasers are roundly celebrated

parts.words: Mrs Giles's chasers are roundly celebrated
parts.note: Farmer Giles is the stock English farmer; the farmer's wife is chased in a nursery rhyme often sung as a round

explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a stock name for an English farmer, so Mrs Giles is the farmer's wife who chases them with a carving knife; the nursery rhyme is sung as a round, hence 'roundly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme three sightless rodents run after the farmer's wife, and the song is a well-known round.

clue.text: Hercules for instance detailed to do some tailing?

explanation.surface: A strongman assigned to follow someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's sleuth; a private eye who 'tails' a suspect is shadowing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Poirot is an example of a sleuth, and a sleuth is the person assigned to shadow a suspect.

clue.text: Political VIP -one's seen in church

explanation.surface: An important politician noticed at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department head holds this title, as does a clergyman who serves a congregation.

clue.text: Bad for example having one boy at a cathedral city out of wedlock

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
I is the Roman numeral for one
Tim is a boy's name
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A wicked child born to unmarried parents in a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A child born to unmarried parents was described as born unlawfully, outside marriage.

clue.text: Element number three (or, shortly, fifty-one)

parts.note: the element with atomic number three has the chemical symbol Li, and LI is also the Roman numeral for fifty-one

explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' points to the element's abbreviation, its symbol Li, which read as Roman numerals is 51.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest metal has atomic number three in the periodic table.

clue.text: We might perhaps call tea milky

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version, so the letters of the words that follow may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that tea could be described as milky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CALL TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal is the scientific adjective for anything relating to or resembling milk.

clue.text: Old" Bill ? Not' Bairns-father's, but his opponent

definitions.text: Old" Bill ? Not' Bairns-father's, but his opponent

parts.words: Old" Bill ? Not' Bairns-father's, but his opponent
parts.note: Old Bill was Bruce Bairnsfather's walrus-moustached cartoon soldier of the First World War; the enemy's Bill was the German emperor, Wilhelm

explanation.walkthrough: Bairnsfather's cartoon Old Bill was a British Tommy; the 'Bill' he fought against was Wilhelm II, known in Britain as Kaiser Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm II, the German emperor, was nicknamed Kaiser Bill by the British in the First World War.

clue.text: How actors perform parts (lest they be all. Greek to us ?)

definitions.text: How actors perform parts (lest they be all. Greek to us ?)

parts.words: How actors perform parts (lest they be all. Greek to us ?)
parts.note: actors render their roles, and something 'all Greek to us' needs translating

explanation.walkthrough: The verb covers both an actor's rendering of a role and translating a foreign language, which is why 'all Greek to us' is in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors render a role in their own way, and translators render an unintelligible language into one we understand.

clue.text: Haggard horseman

explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines, so Rider is his middle name; it also names someone on horseback.

clue.text: Chesterton's cowardly 5 dn gets drunk

explanation.surface: A writer's cowardly scoundrel ends up intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton's song begins 'Cocoa is a cad and coward'; 5 down is CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton mocked the hot chocolate drink as a cad and coward, and that drink is something people consume.

clue.text: But this man wasn't Abel in the film'

definitions.text: But this man wasn't Abel in the film'

parts.words: But this man wasn't Abel in the film'
parts.note: Abel was the ... man in Genesis after Adam and Cain, but the film The ... Man is about Harry Lime

explanation.walkthrough: Counting Adam, Cain and Abel, Abel was the third man in the Bible; in Carol Reed's 1949 film The Third Man it is Harry Lime instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title supplies the ordinal that fills in 'The ... Man'.

clue.text: Fish one catches in wicker baskets

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one
nets means catches, as in nets a fish

explanation.surface: An angler's fish caught in wicker creels.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle for a baby, a basket-like bed.

clue.text: Busybody, one of Tennyson's innumerable murmurers

explanation.surface: A meddler is one of a poet's countless whisperers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's line from The Princess is 'the murmuring of innumerable bees'.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy insect of the hive is proverbial for industry, and Tennyson wrote of the murmuring of innumerable ones.

clue.text: About the Walrus — what he felt after eating oysters?

definitions.text: what he felt after eating oysters?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
morse is an old word for walrus

explanation.surface: In Lewis Carroll's poem the Walrus eats the trusting young oysters and then weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass the Walrus weeps for the oysters he has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt and regret for a wrong done is what the weeping Walrus showed after his meal.

clue.text: Inhabitant died before Pickwick's man

indicators.note: before puts the letter for died ahead of the servant's name

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies
Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's manservant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A resident who died before Mr Pickwick's servant did.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of a place lives or abides there.
